question: What is the usual next-token objective when training many large language models?
correctAnswer: Predict the next token given prior tokens in the sequence
incorrectAnswers: Predict only the first token of a document
Predict the sum of all token IDs
Predict a single fixed label for every input
explanation: Autoregressive language models are trained to estimate conditional probabilities of the next token given the preceding context.

question: Which architecture introduced scaled dot-product self-attention as the core building block for many modern LLMs?
explanation: The Transformer model relies on attention to relate all positions to each other in parallel rather than sequential recurrence.

question: What does the context window of an LLM limit?
correctAnswer: How many tokens the model can attend to in one forward pass
incorrectAnswers: How many users can log in at once
The size of the training dataset on disk
The number of programming languages it knows
explanation: Attention and memory are computed over a bounded number of tokens, so longer prompts and outputs must fit within that window.

question: Compared with only prompting, what does supervised fine-tuning on labeled examples change?
correctAnswer: The model weights to better match the target task or style
incorrectAnswers: Only the font size of the output
explanation: Fine-tuning updates parameters using task-specific data so behavior shifts beyond what fixed prompts alone can achieve.

question: At decoding time, raising the softmax temperature typically does what to token sampling?
correctAnswer: Makes the distribution flatter so outputs become more random
incorrectAnswers: Forces the model to repeat one token forever
explanation: Higher temperature scales logits before softmax, spreading probability mass and increasing diversity of sampled tokens.

question: In retrieval-augmented generation, what extra step happens before the model writes an answer?
correctAnswer: Relevant documents or passages are retrieved from a store and conditioned as context
incorrectAnswers: The prompt is encrypted with AES only
explanation: RAG grounds answers by fetching external text so the model can cite or reason over fresher or private knowledge sources.

question: ChatGPT reads and writes text in small chunks called what?
explanation: AI chatbots split text into chunks called tokens. In English, one token is about 4 characters, or roughly three-quarters of a word.
wowLine: In English, one token is about 4 characters, or roughly three-quarters of a word.

question: A "7B" AI model has 7 billion of what?
explanation: Parameters are the numbers a model learns during training. At 16-bit precision each takes 2 bytes, so 7 billion parameters need about 14 GB of memory.
wowLine: Stored at 16-bit precision, 7 billion parameters take about 14 GB of memory just to load.

question: When a chatbot confidently states something false, it is called what?
explanation: Language models predict likely words rather than look facts up, so they can produce fluent statements that are wrong.
wowLine: Chatbots predict likely words instead of looking facts up, so they can sound sure and still be wrong.

question: What does the T in GPT stand for?
explanation: GPT stands for Generative Pre-trained Transformer. The Transformer design comes from the 2017 paper Attention Is All You Need.
wowLine: The Transformer design was introduced in a 2017 Google paper titled "Attention Is All You Need".

question: What does LLM stand for in AI?
explanation: An LLM is a language model with a very large number of parameters, trained on huge amounts of text. GPT-3 had 175 billion parameters.
wowLine: The 2020 model GPT-3 had 175 billion parameters, far more than any earlier language model.

question: How much text an AI model can consider at once is called its what?
explanation: The context window is measured in tokens and covers your prompt, any documents you add and the reply. Some models accept about 200,000 tokens.
wowLine: Some models can take in about 200,000 tokens at once, roughly the length of a long novel.

question: Turning an AI's temperature setting up makes its answers more what?
explanation: Temperature controls randomness when the model picks each next token. Low values give focused, repeatable answers and high values give more variety.
wowLine: At temperature 0 a model gives nearly the same answer every time. Higher settings add variety.

question: Which company launched ChatGPT in November 2022?
explanation: OpenAI released ChatGPT as a free research preview on 30 November 2022.
wowLine: ChatGPT reached an estimated 100 million users within about two months of launch.
